title: PR review action map & quick triage scratch
content:
Goal: quick personal map for PR #4567 review (runtime hotfix + small refactor). Use this as the single place to capture action items and accept/reject criteria before posting review comments.

Context (high level):
- PR touches kv-cache eviction + small reshuffle of the kernel selection logic (runtime/kernel_selector.*).
- Perf microbench in PR shows 5-8% regression on 512-step median latency in staging (see bench artifacts attached).
- Author: @suresh; flagged by canary after deploy.
- Linked jira INF-3421 (eviction behavior + regression triage).

Quick read notes (first pass):
- Changes appear logically isolated but there are three hotspots:
  1) eviction ordering logic (Lru -> MRU subtle switch), comments unclear (no unit tests).
  2) kernel priority list refactor (reorders fallback choices).
  3) new flag `prefer_ram_kv` added, default true; intended to reduce GPU mem pressure but not fully gated.

Immediate concerns to call out in review (priority):
- Repro determinism: is the regression deterministic or telemetry sampling artifact? Add CI job that runs the perf microbench with the same seed and dataset.
- Safety: default true for `prefer_ram_kv` — needs explicit rollout plan + feature flag gating (dedicated/dry-run).
- Correctness: eviction path doesn't update the metrics counter in one branch (missing increment when evicting from shard X). That will silently hide regressions.

Accept/Reject checklist (what I need to see before approving):
- [ ] Reproduce perf regression locally (bench command + artifacts in PR). If reproduced, add a short blurb in PR explaining root cause or revert candidate.
- [ ] Add a unit test for eviction ordering (edge cases: single-shard wrap-around, concurrent evict+insert).
- [ ] Add telemetry increment for eviction counter in the missing branch.
- [ ] Make `prefer_ram_kv` behind runtime config and set default to false for hosted; document intended rollout in PR description.
- [ ] Add changelog line (internal) + note for SRE on capacity impact.
- [ ] Confirm kernel priority reorder is a pure refactor (no behavioral change) or add a rationale in comments.

Action items with quick estimates (for owning/author):
- Add unit test for eviction ordering (0.5–1d).
- Add telemetry fix + unit (0.25–0.5d).
- Add perf reproducer and run CI bench (0.25d + CI time).
- Wrap `prefer_ram_kv` behind config + doc (0.25–0.5d).
- If perf persists, revert kernel reorder as quick mitigation (0.25d).

Notes to self (debugting plan):
- Run bench with the exact model+sequence used in canary (512-step median). Use the harness in /bench/kv-cache and seed=42.
- Dump memory+eviction logs in staging when reproducing (enable low-level debug for 1 minute window).
- Compare trace of kernel selection decisions between main and this branch (trace id X).

Potential non-blocking suggestions (post-merge follow-ups):
- Add integ test that runs workload with `prefer_ram_kv` toggled to validate perf/cost tradeoffs.
- Add a short note in Optimize docs about when to prefer RAM KV vs GPU (cost signals).
- Consider moving kernel priority list to a small json config so future reorderings are obvious and covered by config validation.

Open questions for the author (leave as review comments):
- Why default = true for prefer_ram_kv? Was there a customer use-case driving this or is it an optimization experiment?
- Are there cases where eviction ordering change could affect correctness (e.g., pinned keys)?
- Are we confident the kernel priority reordering won't change path for small sequence lengths?

Draft review comment (copy/paste friendly):
> Thanks for the PR — good catch on the memory path. I ran a first pass and have a few blocking items before I can approve: I can reproduce a median latency regression in staging benchmarks; please add the perf reproducer + CI job, add a unit test exercising the eviction order edge-cases, and restore telemetry for the eviction counter (missing increment in one branch). Also please gate the new prefer_ram_kv flag behind runtime config and default it to false for hosted until we have a rollout plan documented. Once those are in, I can re-run the microbench and re-review.

Follow-up tracking (my personal checklist):
- [ ] Confirm author pushed fixes (watch PR + GH notifications).
- [ ] After merge, watch canary for 24h, monitor eviction_counter and median latency.
- [ ] Add short retro note to INF-3421 about missed telemetry and testing gap.

Quick links / commands I keep reusing:
- Local perf repro: ./bench/run.sh --suite=kv-eviction --model=rwkv-15b --seq=512 --seed=42
- CI bench job: bench/kvcache-staging (artifact path: /artifacts/bench/pr-4567/* )
- Trace compare snippet: python tools/trace_diff.py --left main.trace --right pr4567.trace

Random scratch lines (notes-to-self, ignore in PR comment):
- Could we add a small invariant assert in eviction path to detect ordering flips early? Cheap check.
- If author pushes revert to kernel reorder, consider pairing with a smaller canary window + perf metric anomaly alert.

End of scratch. Use this to craft the final review comment and to track followups. Keep as my single source of truth for this PR until resolved.

-- Emmett H.
